The paper proposes an operator-splitting and matrix-based numerical scheme to model solidification and macro-segregation processes.
The scheme avoids non-linear systems and is fully decoupled, leading to a linear solution process.
The combination of vectorization and forward equation-based matrix assembly techniques enhances the implementability of the scheme, especially for 3D applications.
The energy equation is solved using a two-step operator-splitting approach to accurately capture latent heat release during phase change.
The matrix-based approach for the solute transport equation avoids auxiliary terms required in traditional methods.
The spatial discretization uses a staggered grid approach, with velocity components defined on cell edges and scalar variables defined at cell centers.
The scheme is validated through a comprehensive set of 2D and 3D benchmark cases.
The numerical results demonstrate the scheme's ability to accurately predict and capture physical phenomena such as channel segregation, freckle formation, edge effects, and 3D effects.
The paper responds to a call for contributions to benchmark analysis of solidification and segregation problems.
The proposed scheme is designed to be efficient and implementable, making it suitable for a wide range of applications involving solidification and macro-segregation processes.
